questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This field shows the two compartments of the testis, the seminiferous tubules and the intervening connective tissue containing the interstitial cells of Leydig in the center of the field.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These testosterone-secreting cells are located in the intervening connective tissue between the seminiferous tubules of the testis. Due to the presence of lipid droplets, they have a foamy-appearing cytoplasm which is characteristic of steroid-secreting cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These cells are tall columnar cells in the seminiferous epithelium. Each has an oval-shaped nucleus that is oriented perpendicular to the basement membrane of the seminiferous tubule. The nuclear envelope often shows infoldings, and the nucleolus is prominent.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The mediastinum is formed from the tunica albuginea, a dense irregular connective tissue capsule that surrounds the entire testis. The connective tissue of the tunic penetrates the posterior surface of the testis and houses the rete testis, a network of passageways that first receives the sperm from the seminiferous tubules.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The head of the epididymis contains efferent ducts and the beginning of the single, highly coiled duct of the epididymis into which they drain. These ducts can be distinguished by their luminal outlines: efferent ducts appear scalloped; the duct of the epididymis outline is smooth.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These cells lie directly on the basement membrane of the epithelium of the seminiferous tubule. Spermatogonia divide by mitosis to perpetuate themselves or to generate primary spermatocytes.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These cells are generated by mitotic division of the spermatogonia and are probably the cells that pass through the blood-testis barrier. Their nuclei are the largest in the seminiferous epithelium, approximately one and one-half times larger than those of spermatogonia, and contain readily visible chromosomes. The cells remain arrested in prophase for about 1/3 of the spermatogenic process.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These cells lie closer to the lumen than primary or secondary spermatocytes and are quite numerous. Their nuclei are condensed and spherical and are smaller than the nuclei of spermatogonia. They are formed by the second meiotic division of secondary spermatocyte and are haploid.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Efferent ducts are located in the head of the epididymis. They are characterized by a scalloped epithelium, due to the presence of both tall and short cells. Some cells posses cilia, the only place cilia are present in the male reproductive tract.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These tubules lie in the mediastinum of the testis and exit through tunica albuginea into the head of the epididymis. They are characterized by having a low cuboidal epithelium, which abuts abruptly with the scalloped epithelium of the efferent ducts. They connect with the straight portions of the seminiferous tubules (tubuli recti).

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The epididymis lies at the posterior aspect of the testis and contains the efferent ducts and the single, highly coiled duct of the epididymis.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The duct of the epididymis is characterized by its smooth, regular luminal surface, in contrast to the scalloped outline of the efferent ducts. Note the tall stereocilia that project into the lumen of the duct. This epithelium is most highly developed in the region of the duct located in the head of the epididymis.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The coni vasculosi are located in the head of the epididymis. Each consists of a coiled efferent duct, the surrounding connective tissue and accompanying vasculature. The individual efferent ducts in each of these structures drain into the single duct of the epididymis.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the tubular structures shown in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The duct of the epididymis is characterized by its smooth, regular luminal surface and the presence of tall stereocilia. The epithelium is pseudostratified and, thus, both tall cells, which reach the surface, and shorter basal cells are present.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Stereocilia are actually tall microvilli, not cilia. They extend into the lumen of the epididymis and aid in absorption of the some of the luminal contents. Like microvilli, they are supported by a core of actin filaments.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The corpora cavernosae are paired cylinders of erectile tissue that are surrounded by a dense connective tissue, the tunica albuginea. They are the major erectile component of the penis.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The corpus spongiosum is an unpaired cylinder of erectile tissue that surrounds the urethra. The tunica albuginea of the corpus spongiosum is less dense than that which surrounds the dorsal corpora cavernosae.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The glands of Littre are mucus-secreting glands which are present along, and empty into, the penile urethra.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Each of the paired seminal vesicles consists of a single, highly coiled tube, which is surrounded by smooth muscle. The epithelium and its underlying connective tissue form complex folds and interconnecting arches diagnostic for this gland.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ shown in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Prostatic concretions (seen in the image on the right) are diagnostic for the prostate. They are composed of glycoprotein and calcify with age. The epithelium lining the glands is pseudostratified with stereocilia.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The prostate gland consists of 30-50 individual tubuloalveolar glands. A fibromuscular coat surrounds each gland, aiding in the propulsion of the prostatic secretions. The prostate gland surrounds the prostatic portion of the urethra (center of the section), into which each of the glands empties individually.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Each of the paired seminal vesicles consists of a single, highly coiled tube, which is surrounded by smooth muscle. The epithelium and its underlying connective tissue form complex folds and interconnecting arches diagnostic for this gland.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The spermatic artery is located within the spermatic cord which also contains the highly muscular ductus deferens (upper left). Surrounding the testicular artery is a system of veins called the pampiniform plexus. The cooler blood in veins returning from the testis serves to lower the temperature of the arterial blood to maintain conditions necessary for sperm production.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Late spermatids are completing the process of spermiogenesis, a cytomorphological differentiation from round, early spermatids to become spermatozoa. Late spermatids remain attached to Sertoli cells and possess a highly thin heterochromatic nucleus and elaborate a long flagellum. Once released from the Sertoli cell, the cells is referred as a spermatozoa.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This is a Masson trichrome-stained section of the ductus deferens. The highly muscular wall of the ductus deferens has three layers of smooth muscle, inner and outer longitudinal and middle circular, whose combined peristaltic actions propel the sperm out of the body.
